condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

Output 1.1 National strategy on inter-agency collaboration and intelligence sharing for combatting wildlife crime is developed and implementation started
• Collaborative efforts between DWNP and Department of Prosecution has been established, during the first data collection after project reset, there has adequate improvement on the availability of wildlife crime statistics that were channelled to DWNP. Although electronic system has not been developed due to failure in developing the ICT system and equipping it, to monitor changes over time in prosecution and convictions as a percentage of arrests, and length of awaiting trial periods • The establishment of one Joint Operational Centre (JOC) has been initiated the previous reporting to contribute to project Output 2.5: Legal and regulatory frameworks, policies and institutions enabled to ensure the conservation, sustainable use, and access and benefit sharing of natural resources, biodiversity and ecosystems, in line with international conventions and national legislation. The procurement of materials to support implementation of the NAPS, which include support to the establishment of the JOC, the Intelligence Diffusion Centres (IDCs), and Forward Operating Bases (Fobs) has been completed. In the reporting period The expected-on boarding of JOC ICT specialist failed to attract a qualified consultant and is yet to be readvertised in 2023. The ICT expert is expected to facilitate development of real time ICT system which will operationalize the JOC with linkages to the IDCs and strengthen real time data collection. • A stakeholder workshop for NAPS validation and Implementation was held on 14 and 15 December 2022 in Gantsi. The workshop was attended by about 30 people composed of representatives of Law enforcement agencies, National Anti-Poaching Coordinating Committee and Chairpersons of District Anti-poaching. The workshop was aimed at briefing the attendees about the role the will play in implementing the actions recommended in the strategy.

Output 4.1 , 4.2, & 4.3 Through the project Gendermainstreaming strategy the project undertook the following to address the gender inequalities, empower women. • As part signature solution: gender and poverty, All projects’ procurements for bushfire management in Component 3 were reserved and awarded to women in the poverty eradication programme, for women empowerment and local empowerment. A total of 4 vendors were issued with PO amounting to $7000 • The ProJet continually cconfronts the structural obstacles to gender equality and strengthening women’s economic empowerment and leadership by extending invitation to all village leadership and village extension committee. The project supported gender balance by urging CBO members to have equal representation or gender balances on all training through invitations i.e., for Bush fire management, Gendermainstreaming. Attendance from CBOS members has reflected otherwise where women who are caregivers declined to attend. Technical Support will continue to be provided, with special attention to sensitizing the project implementing partners in the community for the need to increase womens participation in decision making bodies. The project provided a Gendermainstreaming training to 23 females and 15 males representing the 6 project sites, to Mainstreaming gender equality considerations CBO institutional practices and gender-based violence. Undertaking specific interventions to support GEWE. • Women groups were also targeted by the Project in the ILUMP community consultations to gather data on land issues that affect them directly as primary land users and mass harvesters of veldt products, use of natural resources and conflicting land uses that disadvantage them so that they can be factored in the development of ILUMP. • All consultancy advertisement were specific urge women to apply and assured applicants that, the project provides equal opportunity to both men and women. • The project further has provided 45 % women and 55 % males of SLM i.e., HRM, Bush fire management, Gendermainstreaming and charcoal production. • To strengthen the project performance, M&E for results the project has provided capacity building activities for project IPS and focal points to strengthen their understanding on the revised project results framework and leading the project to achieve its expected outcomes. • The project management unit has participated in the GWP knowledge and lessons sharing platform by attending 15 webinars, in 2022. Also, the project and Ips have incorporated best practises in training of communities and ILUMP development as well fast-tracking progress after MTR. The project manager and Ips attended the study tour and GWP annual conference where by there was Capacity development of capturing and sharing lessons, Presentation of lessons learned in MTR out come and project reset opportunity to address challenges in project implementation; Visit to Masai mara national park and learn about the community conservancy models and their contribution to conservation and law enforcement by so doing the project attained its end of project target of 5 lessons shared.
Project reset The project undertook a successful project reset which was necessitated by the independent Mid-Term review (MTR) of the project in June 2021 found that “All components are currently behind what was envisaged in the Project Document and what might be reasonably expected by the mid-term. The re-set consultancy was designed to help unblock this situation and seek the GEF’s approval for any adjustments that might need to be made in the process, before proceeding with the FPIC and associated safeguards processes. The rese documents were approved in August 2022 and all project activities resumed.
The project also completed the FPIC process FPIC survey was done and completed on the 22nd July and the consultation was done in all 15 villages which were targeted. Out of the 15 villages consulted 12 gave full consent to the project activities, while 3 villages, West Hanahai, Kacgae, and Monnong, gave conditional consent with the request that they be provide with more information regarding: *Aspects of project implementation arrangement, *The selection criteria of the implementing partners, *The role of the partners, and *More information on the amount of funding going to the project activities as compared to funds going to the IP.
